text:
tom: heads-up — product is consolidating Starter+ into a single Starter tier next quarter. want a quick headroom sanity check for eu-west and us-west GPU pools. expected shift: ~40% of Starter Pro traffic -> Starter (higher qps), and ~10% of free-tier churn back to Starter after promo stops. can we model a reasonable worst-case?

aisha: ok. rough ask: will this change increase small-request qps (short seq) or long-run chat sessions?

lee: mostly short requests. product says average tokens/request will drop from 120 -> 60 but requests/sec up ~2.2x for Starter routes. throughput profile moves left (seq len shorter) which helps capacity per-GPU, but concurrency increases.

jess: product note: rollout will also raise per-account rate limit from 30 -> 60 rpm for Starter during a 2-week promo window. goal is smoother upgrade flow.

sanford: finance flag — if we need to pre-provision reserved capacity, what are ballpark committed spend delta? also list which regions need headroom first.

lee: did a quick sim (very rough) using last 30d qps baseline + 2.2x uplift on Starter routes and 10% reactivation from free. result: eu-west GPU-hours/day +18%, us-west +24%, ap-south negligible. caveat: if concurrency spike > 2x at peak minute, tail latency will degrade.

capacity-sim-bot: summary report uploaded: https://artifacts/redwood/capacity-sims/2025-03-rate-plan-consol/summary.csv :heavy_check_mark:

lee: pasted core numbers:
```
scenario, eu_west_gpu_hours, us_west_gpu_hours, peak_concurrency_multiplier
baseline, 420, 560, 1.0
consol+promo, 496, 694, 1.9
consol+promo+promo-end-churn, 515, 715, 2.1
```

aisha: ok that looks ~right. ops notes: current autoscaler has a scale-up cool-down of 90s and we limit per-pool max-concurrency-per-gpu to 48. with 2.1x peak we may hit the soft cap; recommend temporary bump to 64 for Starter pool during rollout and shorten cool-down to 30s.

jess: can we do canary routing? route 10% of Starter traffic to a heavier-quantized, cheaper model variant in us-west to soak traffic while keeping latency SLOs. then fallback.

lee: yes. perf tradeoff: quantized variant saves ~22% GPU-hours but adds ~40ms p90 for short requests. overall latency still < our 200ms p95 SLO at expected loads.

sanford: if we accept the quantized canary and bump reserved capacity in us-west for safety, cost delta estimate: +$14k/mo reserved vs +$27k/mo on-demand if we fail to reserve (estimate). prefer reserved if committed.

tom: action items:
- aisha to roll temporary autoscaler param changes in staging and smoke test at 11:30 PT tomorrow.
- lee to run minute-level sim with 5-min tail events and export updated CSV.
- jess to configure 10% canary route and quantized variant in us-west.
- sanford to confirm finance approval for up to $20k/mo reserved headroom if needed.

aisha: noted. i'll post the staging runbook in #eng-infra-runbooks before smoke.

lee: i'm going to run a tight minute-level sim now, will post results in thread.

capacity-sim-bot: minute-sim complete. peak_concurrency hit 2.08x at 2025-03-18T17:42Z. details -> https://artifacts/redwood/capacity-sims/2025-03-rate-plan-consol/minute-sim.json

tom: thanks — looks like we should be fine with the autoscaler tweaks + canary. if finance OKs the reserved headroom we'll schedule the rollout window. :thumbsup:
